title: Crosses and Circles
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/eca2f836e6fafe6d7664ef9cfe16a6ab772f2dc0.png)An unusual game of tic-tac-toe.

Your friend watched some video about Connect Four and memorized the winning strategy for the starting player. What a loser! Whatever they are saying sounds about as relevant to your life as this paragraph is to the problem statement. Apparently, someone found a weak solution to Connect Four which can be compressed to just $150\,\textrm{kB}$ and requires no game tree search.

To get them off their high horse, you challenge them to a real game. You pull out a piece of A4 graph paper and explain: "We will take turns picking any unpicked cell. The first player to get three consecutive cells in any row, column, or diagonal wins. I will start." Your friend is barely listening, but this is not just regular tic-tac-toe: you are playing on the whole paper. Convert your winning advantage.

## Interaction

This is an interactive problem. Your submission will be run against an interactor, which reads from the standard output of your submission and writes to the standard input of your submission. This interaction needs to follow a specific protocol:

There is no initial input as you make the first move.

On each of your turns, print one line with two integers $r$ and $c$ ($1 \le r \le 59$, $1 \le c \le 42$), the row and column of the cell you pick. The cell must not have been picked before.

After each of your moves, the interactor will respond with one line with two integers $r'$ and $c'$ ($0 \le r' \le 59$, $0 \le c' \le 42$).

- If $r' = c' = 0$, the interaction is over. This happens if you won on your last move, made an illegal move, or your friend can win with their next move. Your program should terminate immediately.
- Otherwise, $1 \le r' \le 59$ and $1 \le c' \le 42$. This means that your friend picked the cell in row $r'$ and column $c'$. It is guaranteed that neither player has picked this cell before. It is now your turn again, and the interaction continues from there.

The interactor is adaptive, so your friend's moves will depend on all previous moves.

Make sure you **flush** the standard output after every output. For example, you can use `fflush(stdout)` in C++, `System.out.flush()` in Java, `sys.stdout.flush()` in Python, `std::io::stdout().flush()` in Rust, and `hFlush stdout` in Haskell.

A testing tool is provided to help you develop your solution.
statementZhMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/eca2f836e6fafe6d7664ef9cfe16a6ab772f2dc0.png)一场不寻常的井字棋游戏。

你的朋友看了一段关于四子棋的视频，并记住了先手的必胜策略。真逊！他们说的那些东西与你的生活有多大关系，大概就和这一段与题目本身有多大关系一样。据说，有人找到了四子棋的一个弱解，可以压缩到仅 $150\,\textrm{kB}$，而且不需要搜索博弈树。

为了杀杀他们的威风，你向他们发起了一场真正的对局。你拿出一张 A4 方格纸，解释道：“我们轮流选择任意一个尚未被选过的格子。谁先在任意一行、一列或一条斜线上占据三个连续的格子，谁就获胜。我先手。”你的朋友几乎没在听，但这可不是普通的井字棋：你们要在整张纸上进行游戏。将你的必胜优势转化为胜利吧。

## 交互

这是一道交互题。你提交的程序将与交互器对局，交互器会读取你程序的标准输出，并向你程序的标准输入写入内容。交互必须遵循以下协议：

由于你先手，因此没有初始输入。

每次轮到你时，输出一行，包含两个整数 $r$ 和 $c$（$1 \le r \le 59$, $1 \le c \le 42$），表示你选择的格子所在的行和列。该格子必须此前未被选过。

在你每次落子后，交互器会回复一行，包含两个整数 $r'$ 和 $c'$（$0 \le r' \le 59$, $0 \le c' \le 42$）。

- 如果 $r' = c' = 0$，则交互结束。当你在刚才的落子后获胜、进行了非法落子，或你的朋友能在下一步获胜时，就会出现这种情况。你的程序应立即终止。
- 否则，$1 \le r' \le 59$ 且 $1 \le c' \le 42$。这表示你的朋友选择了第 $r'$ 行、第 $c'$ 列的格子。保证双方此前都没有选过这个格子。现在再次轮到你，交互继续。

交互器具有自适应性，因此你朋友的落子会取决于此前的所有落子。

请确保每次输出后都**刷新**标准输出。例如，你可以在 C++ 中使用 `fflush(stdout)`，在 Java 中使用 `System.out.flush()`，在 Python 中使用 `sys.stdout.flush()`，在 Rust 中使用 `std::io::stdout().flush()`，在 Haskell 中使用 `hFlush stdout`。

题目提供了一个测试工具，帮助你开发解法。
